title: Dispatch: per-clause ownership of dawn/dusk dice charge recharge without depletion rules (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for eshyra-9ooo. Read `bd show eshyra-9ooo`, AGENTS.md, docs/importer-fix-protocol.md, docs/rules-pack-compiler.md, and the eshyra-7gkh.1 precedent (thaw note docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/2026-10-26-eshyra-7gkh-1-dawn-economy-readiness.md; per-clause ownership code in scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemCompiler.ts ~line 950 beside activationOwned/grantOwned). Worktree/branch named after your bead, cut from parent branch eshyra-9ooo.

FACTS (verified by supervisor on main 2f747ddf): hook {F5,'magic-item-usage-recharge'} (assigned in scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemChargeEconomies.ts clausesFor ~line 967, on c1-economy-<id> and c1-operation-<id> clauses) is carried by 207 clauses of 53 items and NOT landed globally (shapes include d20 destruction/regain-on-20 depletion rules, no reset, 7-day resets). useItem (src/state/itemState.ts costAmount ~1883) executes fixed positive-integer costs and 'variable' costs from args.costs.<economy> (positive integer); dice-derived costs throw. The reset executor (src/state/itemResetExecutor.ts resetAmount/validateResetShape) executes dawn and dusk resets whose amount is 'all' or a dice string (seeded RNG).

DECISION (supervisor): own the hook PER CLAUSE by economy shape, not globally. Predicate (put it in a small exported function, documented like creatureGrantLifecycleOwned, with the rationale): an economy is recharge-owned when kind === 'charges', charges.max is a positive integer, reset is EXACTLY one entry {at:'dawn'|'dusk', amount: <dice string the executor accepts> | 'all'} with no other keys, and there is NO onDepleted (any depletion consequence — d20 destruction, becomes nonmagical/inert/destroyed, loseProperty, regainOn — keeps the clause pending, since that is a different contract). A c1-economy-<id> clause loses the hook when its economy is recharge-owned; a c1-operation-<id> clause loses it when every cost of the operation is on a recharge-owned economy and every cost amount is a positive integer or 'variable'. The hook stays on every other clause. Do NOT add it to LANDED_MAGIC_ITEM_ENGINE_HOOKS.
Before relying on it, VERIFY in the runtime that a dice regain is capped at charges.max (and fix only if it is not, with a test) and that a 'variable' spend larger than the remaining charges is refused.
Pipes of the Sewers is the bead's subject: its c1-economy-charges and c1-operation-call-rat-swarms should go green; its operation stays refused because m4 (no printed ending) remains engine-pending — that is the truthful outcome; say so. Report the exact list of items/clauses that change and any newly ready operations.

EVIDENCE (real pack, unmodified, no waiver): R1 a recharge-owned item with a ready operation (pick one whose operation becomes newly ready, if any; else use the economy directly through useItem/reset executor on the real record): spend charges with use_item, cross a dawn (or dusk for Robe of Stars only if it qualifies) boundary with a seeded rng, assert the regain equals the roll capped at max. R2 Pipes: a 'variable' spend of 2 then of 2 again with 1 remaining is refused; dawn regains 1d3 capped at 3. R3 compiler: counterfactuals — the same shape with onDepleted, with a 7-day reset, or with two reset entries keeps the hook. Negative-proof each once.
R Regenerate canonical pack (`npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/`), `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`, regenerate the semi-structured inventory via writeCommittedOutputs() (packages/core/scripts/inventory-semi-structured-boundary.ts, throwaway tsx script outside the repo), thaw note docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/2026-10-31-eshyra-9ooo-dawn-dice-recharge-ownership.md (format of the 7gkh one, exact counts). Update srdGeneratedPack.test.ts pins and any READY operation list to ACTUAL values; never weaken other pins.

PROCESS: `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root must pass BEFORE committing; commit on your branch (message starts with your bead id); report via `bd update <your bead> --append-notes "..."`; follow-ups via bd create; `bd close <your bead>`.
